question: Banned providers still in the drug-money stream: OIG-excluded providers (LEIE) who received pharma/device industry payments (CMS Open Payments 2022-2024)
finding: 439 OIG-excluded providers received 2,938 industry payments totaling $1.03M in program years ON OR AFTER their exclusion year (out of 799 excluded NPIs matched to $6.26M of payments overall); fraud-conviction exclusions (1128a1) alone account for 216 after-exclusion provider-years and $264k, and one 1128b7 (fraud/kickback) neurologist took in $620k across 2022-2023 after a 2021 exclusion.
chart: plotly scatter (strip/jitter): x = PAY_YEAR - EXCLUSION_YEAR (years since exclusion), y = TOTAL_DOLLARS (log scale), color = AFTER_EXCLUSION_FLAG (or EXCLUSION_TYPE), size = N_PAYMENTS; alternative: stacked bar of after-exclusion dollars by EXCLUSION_TYPE.
caveats: Year-grain comparison only: a payment in the same calendar year as the exclusion may predate the exclusion date; flag uses payment program year >= exclusion year.
after_exclusion_flag also requires the provider not reinstated before the payment year; reinstatement dates present for only a minority.
Only ~10% of LEIE rows carry a usable NPI (8,503 distinct), so this undercounts excluded providers substantially.
Open Payments coverage here is program years 2022, 2023, 2024 only.
Receiving an industry payment while excluded is not itself illegal; exclusion bars federal-program billing. Association/receipt shown, no wrongdoing implied.
The single largest row ($3.08M, 2024, excluded 2025) is one pre-exclusion payment, not after-exclusion money.
notable: NPI-level top after-exclusion earner: a South Dakota neurologist excluded 2021 under 1128b7 received $318k (2023) + $302k (2022) = $620k after exclusion.
591 of 1,292 matched provider-years (46%) fall on/after the exclusion year.
Largest single matched payment: $3,082,225 to an Oklahoma family-practice physician in 2024, one year before their 2025 exclusion.
